## Purpose and audience

This manual is for water-resources modelers and climate-risk practitioners who need to understand what a BlueEarth CST assessment represents before using its results.
It describes the present five-workflow engine, its models and data, and the conventions needed to interpret a climate response surface.
For installation and commands, use the [Setup guide](../install.md) and [User guide](../guide/quick-start.qmd).

## Assessment logic

The toolbox supports **bottom-up hydroclimatic stress testing**: vary climate stressors systematically, simulate the hydrological response, and identify combinations that cross a chosen performance threshold.
Temperature and precipitation changes define the main stress-test grid; stochastic weather realizations sample natural variability within that grid.
The retained indicators can be assembled into a climate response map or surface that relates hydrological response to those stressors.
CMIP6 change factors can then be placed in the same space to judge the plausibility of vulnerable conditions.
They do not select or generate the stress-test scenarios.

This is a sensitivity and vulnerability assessment, not a forecast for a particular year or emissions pathway.
Its rapid, globally supported model setup is suited to first-order screening of river-flow risks, including water availability and high-flow concerns.
Investment design and site-specific risk estimates require assessment of local data quality, model skill, decision thresholds, and uncertainty appropriate to the decision.

## Read this manual

1. [Assessment workflow](assessment-workflow.qmd) explains the five stages and their dependencies.
2. [Models and methods](models-and-methods.qmd) explains the hydrological model, weather generation, perturbations, and indicators.
3. [Datasets](datasets.qmd) identifies the role of each data class and what a source change can affect.
4. [Conventions and interpretation](conventions-and-interpretation.qmd) explains periods, units, provenance, climate response surfaces, and limits.

The terminology follows the [2025 CST technical note](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/docs/cst-toolbox-technical-note-2025.md).
That note describes the earlier three-workflow prototype and web application; the pages here describe the current workflow engine.
